key_insight: Feature-space Smoothing (FS) converts any multimodal feature encoder into a smoothed variant that provably limits the effect of adversarial perturbations on feature representations, yielding certified robustness for downstream MLLM predictions.
problem_solved: MLLMs are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations that distort intermediate feature representations and cause incorrect outputs; prior defenses lack theoretical guarantees for multimodal feature robustness.
method: Apply smoothing (noise-averaging) directly in the encoder feature space to produce a smoothed feature extractor that reduces sensitivity to input perturbations.

Derive theoretical certificates that bound how much a feature can be perturbed before the smoothed encoder’s output (and thus downstream prediction) can change — i.e., a provable robustness radius in feature space.
Design FS as a plug-in transformation compatible with existing encoders and LLM heads, enabling certified robustness without redesigning the entire MLLM pipeline.
impact: Gives practitioners a practical, plug-and-play defense with formal guarantees, making multimodal systems more reliable against adversarial attacks and suitable for safety-critical deployments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image/text → feature encoder → Feature-space Smoothing block → LLM head, annotated with a certified radius around smoothed features.
Feature-space visualization (t-SNE/PCA) showing: original features, adversarial-shifted features, and how FS pulls/adapts features back into robust clusters.
Line chart: model accuracy and certified robustness percentage versus perturbation magnitude, comparing baseline vs FS.
Iconic badge/infographic: shield or certificate showing 'provable robustness' and an annotated robustness radius to convey certification intuitively.
paper_title: Provable Robustness in Multimodal Large Language Models via Feature Space Smoothing
paper_authors: Song Xia, Meiwen Ding, Chenqi Kong, Wenhan Yang, Xudong Jiang
